lines: Irregular uterine bleeding and increasing abdominal girth with pelvic fullness
The patient returns for follow-up of her known ovarian malignancy and endometrial carcinoma.
She reports a 6-month history of irregular uterine bleeding and increasing abdominal girth with a sensation of fullness in her pelvis and occasional pelvic pain.
She has a past medical history of hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
- No family history of cardiovascular disease
- No family history of thromboembolic disease
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Librarian.
A palpable, nontender mass is noted in the lower abdomen.
Pelvic examination reveals a firm, irregularly shaped mass arising from the pelvis.
Breast examination shows mild bilateral tenderness without discrete masses or nipple discharge.
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates a 10 cm solid ovarian mass with internal blood flow.
Endometrial biopsy is performed due to the postmenopausal bleeding, which shows a thickened endometrium with no evidence of malignancy.
